cards.name: IVGShape
cards.summary: The Shape object: every drawable thing in a CorelDRAW document (rectangle, ellipse, curve, text, bitmap, group, effect group, guide, the selection itself) is an IVGShape. It carries geometry (position, size, rotation, matrix), styling (Fill, Outline, Transparency), stacking and layer placement, shaping (Weld/Trim/Intersect), live effects (drop shadow, contour, blend, envelope, extrude, lens) and conversion (to curves, to bitmap).
use_for: place and size a logo, badge or price tag at exact page coordinates in a layout
restyle an object's fill/outline and rename it for later lookup in a template
boolean shaping for logos and icons (weld, trim, intersect, fillet/chamfer corners)
add a drop shadow, inner shadow or contour to a headline or product card
convert text to curves or rasterize an object before sending print-ready files
PowerClip a photo inside a frame shape for a poster or social card
avoid: operating on many objects one by one in a loop when a ShapeRange call (ApplyUniformFill, AlignAndDistribute, Group) does it in one step
IVGShape.Group / IVGShape.Combine on a single shape: they act on the current selection; build an IVGShapeRange and call its Group / Combine instead
ConvertToCurves on text that still needs editing: it is one-way, keep a hidden duplicate first
cards.how: Dual dispinterface in VGCore (VGCoreAuto.tlb). A script never creates it directly: it comes back from Layer.CreateRectangle2 / CreateEllipse2 / CreateArtisticText, from ActiveShape / ActiveSelection, from Shapes.Item(i) or ShapeRange.Item(i), or from methods that return a new shape (Duplicate, Clone, Weld, Trim, ConvertToBitmapEx). Type (cdrShapeType) tells which type-specific sub-object (Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon, Curve, Text, Bitmap, Connector) is meaningful. PowerClip is not a Type: any shape can be a PowerClip container, so test Shape.PowerClip itself (expected Nothing when it is not one, unverified).

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: cdrShapeType: check before touching type-specific sub-objects (Text, Curve, Bitmap ...)

key_members.name: Name
key_members.use: read/write object name; set it so later scripts can FindShape by name

key_members.name: LeftX
key_members.use: left edge in document units (also RightX, TopY, BottomY): placement independent of ReferencePoint

key_members.name: SetPosition
key_members.use: move to PositionX, PositionY measured at the document ReferencePoint

key_members.name: SetSize
key_members.use: stretch to Width / Height (either optional)

key_members.name: SetBoundingBox
key_members.use: move and resize into a box in one call, KeepAspect optional

key_members.name: BoundingBox
key_members.use: IVGRect of the shape's bounds without ByRef out-params

key_members.name: RotationAngle
key_members.use: absolute rotation in degrees, read/write

key_members.name: Fill
key_members.use: IVGFill: uniform, fountain, pattern, texture fills

key_members.name: Outline
key_members.use: IVGOutline: width, colour, style, arrows

key_members.name: Duplicate
key_members.use: independent copy offset by OffsetX/OffsetY (default 0, 0)

key_members.name: Weld
key_members.use: union with TargetShape; LeaveSource / LeaveTarget default False

key_members.name: Trim
key_members.use: cut this shape out of TargetShape; LeaveSource default True, LeaveTarget default False

key_members.name: Intersect
key_members.use: new shape from the overlap; LeaveSource / LeaveTarget default True

key_members.name: CreateDropShadow
key_members.use: live drop shadow: Opacity 50, Feather 15, Offset 0,0 by default

key_members.name: CreateContour
key_members.use: live contour (inside/outside steps) around the shape

key_members.name: AddToPowerClip
key_members.use: put this shape inside a container shape (PowerClip)

key_members.name: ConvertToCurves
key_members.use: turn text / primitives into editable curves (one-way)

key_members.name: ConvertToBitmapEx
key_members.use: rasterize to a bitmap shape; Resolution defaults to 72

key_members.name: Delete
key_members.use: remove the shape from the document

gotchas: Coordinates and sizes are in ActiveDocument.Unit, measured from the page's lower-left corner with Y increasing upward (a Photoshop/Illustrator-style top-down Y gives mirrored layouts). Set the unit explicitly at the start of a script; the default for script-created documents may be inches (unverified).

PositionX / PositionY / SetPosition are measured at the document's ReferencePoint, so the same numbers land differently if a script or user changed it; LeftX / TopY / CenterX / SetPositionEx are unambiguous.

GetBoundingBox, GetPosition, GetSize and GetMatrix return values through ByRef parameters (the harvest marks them byref). Late-bound callers such as Python win32com may not get them back; read BoundingBox, LeftX/RightX/TopY/BottomY or SizeWidth/SizeHeight instead (unverified for every binding).

Shaping defaults differ per method: Weld consumes both shapes, Trim keeps the cutter and replaces the target, Intersect keeps both and adds a new shape. Use the returned shape, not the old reference, afterwards.
ConvertToBitmapEx defaults to Resolution 72: pass 300 or more for print. ConvertToCurves and ConvertToBitmap are destructive.

CreateDropShadow with default OffsetX/OffsetY 0 puts the shadow straight behind the object (only the feather shows); pass offsets for a visible cast shadow. The shadow becomes a separate effect object reachable through Effects.
After Delete, Cut, Weld or Combine the old reference is dead; touching it raises an automation error (unverified for every case).
Group and Combine on IVGShape operate on the current selection, not on this shape alone; use ShapeRange.Group / ShapeRange.Combine for predictable results.

Long loops redraw on every change: wrap them in Application.Optimization = True ... False (then ActiveWindow.Refresh) and ActiveDocument.BeginCommandGroup / EndCommandGroup for one undo step; a script that dies with Optimization still True leaves the UI not redrawing.

Shape.Duplicate does not copy a live drop shadow (the duplicate reads Effects.Count 0). CreateDropShadow adds a separate group shape (type 16) that holds the shape and its shadow, so Shape.ConvertToBitmapEx on the shape alone leaves the shadow out: convert the type 16 group. Shape.FlattenEffects on a shadowed star gave a dull indigo shape with no shadow (plan runs 2026-10-15 (print_prep.flatten_transparency)).

Two shadow-type effects on one object replace each other: an inner shadow followed by a drop shadow kept only the drop shadow, so put the second on a duplicate (plan runs 2026-10-15 (text_effects.letterpress)). A drop shadow on a live Contour group follows the inner base shape, not the contour: break the group apart first (plan runs 2026-10-15 (cutout_social.sticker_cutout)).

Break Apart on an extrusion group leaves a type-7 group of the wall faces: Shape.UngroupAll() splits it (Shape.Ungroup() returned None there), then Shape.Weld(target, False, False) over the faces one after another gives one complete shape, where the Weld menu item kept only part of them (plan runs 2026-10-15 (text_effects.long_shadow)).
cards.example:
Dim s As Shape, c As Shape
Set s = ActiveLayer.CreateRectangle2(1, 1, 3, 1.5)
s.Name = "price_tag"
s.Fill.ApplyUniformFill CreateRGBColor(230, 40, 40)
s.RotationAngle = 8
s.CreateDropShadow Opacity:=60, Feather:=10, OffsetX:=0.05, OffsetY:=-0.05
Set c = s.Duplicate(0, -2)
c.SetSize 3, 0.75

review.changes: how: removed PowerClip from the sub-objects selected by Type (cdrShapeType has no PowerClip value); added Polygon/Connector and a note that PowerClip is tested separately.

cards.name: IVGShapeRange
cards.summary: A ShapeRange is a script-held list of shapes (any mix of shape types and layers) that you can transform, style, align, group or combine as one unit. It is what ActiveSelectionRange, Shapes.All, Shapes.FindShapes and Application.CreateShapeRange return, and it does not change the user's selection unless asked.
use_for: recolor every object of a brand element at once (ApplyUniformFill, ApplyFountainFill, SetOutlineProperties)
align and distribute a row of icons, buttons or product shots on a grid
group or combine the parts of a logo lock-up after building it
step-and-repeat a set of objects for labels, tickets or tile patterns
resize or move a whole block of a layout (SizeWidth, SetBoundingBox, Move)
filter a selection down to one shape type (FindAnyOfType) before batch edits
avoid: assuming it tracks the document live: shapes created or deleted after the range was built are not added or removed for you; rebuild it
Delete when you only mean to drop a shape from the list: Delete removes every shape in the range from the document, Remove / RemoveRange only edit the list
relying on it to change what the user sees selected: call CreateSelection or AddToSelection when the UI selection matters
cards.how: Dual dispinterface in VGCore. Reach it from Application.ActiveSelectionRange, Document.SelectionRange, Shapes.All / Range / FindShapes, Shape.DuplicateAsRange / UngroupEx / BreakApartEx, or start empty with Application.CreateShapeRange and fill it with Add / AddRange. Items are 1-based; For Each works through _NewEnum.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of shapes in the list

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: 1-based index or shape name

key_members.name: Add
key_members.use: append one shape to the list

key_members.name: AddRange
key_members.use: append another range

key_members.name: Remove
key_members.use: drop the shape at Index from the list only

key_members.name: Group
key_members.use: group all shapes and return the group shape

key_members.name: Combine
key_members.use: combine all shapes into one curve and return it

key_members.name: ApplyUniformFill
key_members.use: solid fill on every shape (needs an IVGColor)

key_members.name: ApplyFountainFill
key_members.use: gradient fill on every shape

key_members.name: SetOutlineProperties
key_members.use: set width / colour / style etc. on every outline, named args

key_members.name: AlignAndDistribute
key_members.use: align and / or distribute the shapes (MethodH, MethodV, AlignTo)

key_members.name: AlignToShape
key_members.use: align every shape to one key shape

key_members.name: SetBoundingBox
key_members.use: move and resize the whole block into a box

key_members.name: SizeWidth
key_members.use: width of the range's combined bounds, read/write (SizeHeight likewise)

key_members.name: BoundingBox
key_members.use: IVGRect of the combined bounds

key_members.name: FindAnyOfType
key_members.use: sub-range of shapes whose type is in TypeList

key_members.name: Sort
key_members.use: reorder the list with a CQL compare expression

key_members.name: StepAndRepeat
key_members.use: make NumCopies copies at DistanceX / DistanceY

key_members.name: CreateSelection
key_members.use: make this range the UI selection

key_members.name: Delete
key_members.use: delete every shape in the range from the document

gotchas: ActiveSelectionRange is a snapshot taken when you read it; later selection changes do not update it, and reading ActiveSelection instead gives a single Selection Shape whose Shapes are the selected objects.
Delete removes all shapes from the document; DeleteItem(Index) deletes one shape from the document; Remove(Index) / RemoveRange / RemoveAll only change the list.

Group, Combine and ConvertToBitmapEx return a new IVGShape; continue with the returned shape, since the range is not updated to it and its old references may be grouped, merged away or replaced (unverified per method).
Combine merges everything into one curve object with one fill and outline; the other shapes' styles are lost (which shape's style wins is unverified).
Setting SizeWidth or SizeHeight alone stretches the block non-proportionally; use SetSize with both values or SetBoundingBox with KeepAspect.
GetBoundingBox / GetPosition / GetSize use ByRef out-params, awkward from Python win32com; read BoundingBox, LeftX/RightX/TopY/BottomY or CenterX/CenterY instead (unverified for every binding).
Sort takes a CQL comparison of two shapes (written with @shape1 / @shape2, e.g. "@shape1.left < @shape2.left") (unverified).
Split and GetColors return SAFEARRAYs: in VBA a Variant array, in Python a tuple.
cards.example:
Dim sr As ShapeRange, g As Shape
Set sr = ActiveSelectionRange
If sr.Count < 2 Then Exit Sub
sr.ApplyUniformFill CreateRGBColor(0, 90, 160)
sr.SetBoundingBox 1, 1, 6, 2, True
Set g = sr.Group
g.Name = "logo_lockup"

review.changes: summary: dropped the unconfirmed "or pages" mix; gotcha on Group/Combine/ConvertToBitmapEx no longer states as fact that the range still lists the old shapes (marked unverified).

cards.name: IVGShapes
cards.summary: The live Shapes collection owned by a page, layer, group, PowerClip or the selection: it lists the shapes directly inside that container, in stacking order, and offers lookup by index, name, type or a CQL query (FindShape / FindShapes). Converting it to a ShapeRange (All, Range, AllExcluding) is how scripts act on its contents in bulk.
use_for: find a named placeholder (headline, price, photo frame) in a template page and fill it
list everything on a layer before an export or preflight pass
walk the children of a group or PowerClip to restyle them
collect all shapes of one type (text, bitmaps) for batch font or resolution checks
avoid: deleting shapes inside For Each over the same collection: it skips items; loop by index from Count down to 1, or take All first
expecting Count to include objects inside groups: only direct children are counted; use FindShapes with Recursive for nested ones
cards.how: Dual dispinterface in VGCore, read-only container. Reached as Page.Shapes, Layer.Shapes, Shape.Shapes (children of a group, or the selected objects of a Selection Shape) and PowerClip.Shapes. It is live: it reflects shapes added or removed after you read it. Item is 1-based and also accepts a name.

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of direct child shapes

key_members.name: Item
key_members.use: 1-based index or shape name

key_members.name: First
key_members.use: first shape in the collection

key_members.name: Last
key_members.use: last shape in the collection

key_members.name: FindShape
key_members.use: first shape matching Name / Type / StaticID / Query; Recursive defaults True

key_members.name: FindShapes
key_members.use: all shapes matching Name / Type / Query as a ShapeRange; Recursive defaults True

key_members.name: All
key_members.use: snapshot of every shape as a ShapeRange

key_members.name: Range
key_members.use: ShapeRange of the shapes at the given indexes

key_members.name: AllExcluding
key_members.use: ShapeRange of every shape except the given indexes

key_members.name: _NewEnum
key_members.use: makes For Each work

gotchas: Page.Shapes, Layer.Shapes and Shape.Shapes are different scopes: a page's collection spans its layers, a layer's only that layer, a group's only its children.
FindShape / FindShapes search inside groups by default (Recursive defaults True); pass Recursive:=False to stay at the top level.
The Query argument is a CQL expression evaluated per shape (e.g. on @name or @type); a syntax error fails at run time, so test the query on a small page first (unverified error behaviour).

Which item Item("name") returns when several shapes share a name, and whether a missing name raises or returns Nothing, is not confirmed; prefer FindShape(Name:=...) and test for Nothing (unverified).
Indexes follow stacking order and change when shapes are added, deleted or reordered; do not cache an index, cache the shape or its StaticID.
Guidelines and master-layer objects live on their own layers and may appear in page-wide searches (unverified); filter by Type or by Layer.
cards.example:
Dim i As Long, sr As ShapeRange
For i = ActiveLayer.Shapes.Count To 1 Step -1
  If ActiveLayer.Shapes.Item(i).Name = "temp" Then ActiveLayer.Shapes.Item(i).Delete
Next i
Set sr = ActivePage.Shapes.FindShapes(Name:="price")
Debug.Print sr.Count

cards.name: IVGSnapPoint
cards.summary: One snap point of a shape: a position that snapping and connector lines can attach to. cdrPointType lists user, object, bounding-box, edge, free and auto points; the User, Object, BBox and Edge sub-objects hold the type-specific details, and IsMovable / IsDeletable say whether a given point can be moved or deleted.
use_for: add custom anchor points to an icon or diagram block so connector lines attach where you want
read exact corner or centre positions of an object to place callouts, labels or dimension marks
find the point a connector is attached to, then move the attached object precisely
avoid: moving or deleting a snap point without checking IsMovable / IsDeletable: object and bounding-box points follow the shape, move the shape or its nodes instead
using it to edit path geometry: nodes are edited through IVGCurve / IVGNode, a snap point only exposes the Node it sits on
cards.how: Dual dispinterface in VGCore. Reached from a shape's snap-point collection (Shape.SnapPoints, Shape.SnapPointsOfType, Shape.FindSnapPoint by ReferenceData), from SnapPoints.AddUserSnapPoint for a new user point, from the SnapPoints finders (User by ID, Object, BBox, Edge, Auto, FindClosest), and from a connector's StartPoint / EndPoint. Type (cdrPointType) says which of User / Object / BBox / Edge applies.

key_members.name: Type
key_members.use: cdrPointType: which kind of snap point this is

key_members.name: PositionX
key_members.use: X in document units, read/write

key_members.name: PositionY
key_members.use: Y in document units, read/write

key_members.name: SetPosition
key_members.use: move the point to PositionX, PositionY

key_members.name: Move
key_members.use: shift the point by OffsetX, OffsetY

key_members.name: IsMovable
key_members.use: True when Move / SetPosition are allowed

key_members.name: IsDeletable
key_members.use: True when Delete is allowed

key_members.name: Delete
key_members.use: remove the point (user points)

key_members.name: ReferenceData
key_members.use: stable string id; pass to Shape.FindSnapPoint to get the point back later

key_members.name: Shape
key_members.use: the shape the point belongs to

key_members.name: Node
key_members.use: the curve node under the point, if any

key_members.name: User
key_members.use: user-point details: ID (GUID) and AutoSnap

key_members.name: Object
key_members.use: object-point details: its cdrObjectSnapPointType

key_members.name: BBox
key_members.use: bounding-box-point details: which cdrReferencePoint it is

key_members.name: Edge
key_members.use: edge-point details: SegmentIndex and SegmentOffset along the path

key_members.name: Direction
key_members.use: default direction of the point, used when UsesDirection is True (unit not stated in the harvest)

key_members.name: UsesDirection
key_members.use: whether the point uses Direction

gotchas: Only some points can be edited: check IsMovable before Move / SetPosition and IsDeletable before Delete; built-in object and bounding-box points are typically fixed to the shape (unverified for every type).
Only the sub-object that matches Type (User, Object, BBox or Edge) is meaningful; the others are expected to return Nothing (unverified).
Positions are expected to be page coordinates in ActiveDocument.Unit with Y increasing upward, not offsets relative to the shape (unverified).
Store ReferenceData, not a collection index, to find the same point again; indexes can shift as the shape is edited (unverified).
Connector lines attach to snap points: moving or deleting a point a connector uses re-routes or detaches that connector (unverified).
cards.example:
Dim sp As SnapPoint, ref As String
Set sp = ActiveShape.SnapPoints.AddUserSnapPoint(4, 3)
ref = sp.ReferenceData
If sp.IsMovable Then sp.SetPosition 4.5, 3
Set sp = ActiveShape.FindSnapPoint(ref)
Debug.Print sp.PositionX, sp.PositionY

review.changes: summary: listed all cdrPointType kinds (free and auto were missing) and replaced the unconfirmed "user points movable, built-in mostly not" with IsMovable / IsDeletable; how: added the SnapPoints finders; key_members User/Object/BBox/Edge/Direction/UsesDirection now say what the harvest exposes (dropped invented "degrees" and "connector exit direction"); coordinate gotcha marked unverified.
